title: Tech sold off, oil hit $116 and bonds rallied anyway
dek: The Nasdaq fell 4.4% in two weeks while the Dow rose 1.4%. Inflation ran hot, yet investors fled AI stocks for Treasuries and pushed yields down.
summary: Hot inflation, an AI selloff, a flight into Treasuries and $116 Brent. Plus earnings, club news and the week ahead.

briefs.headline: Inflation runs hot
briefs.body: September CPI rose 3.7% from a year earlier, above the 3.6% forecast. Producer prices ran at a 6.3% annual rate, the hottest since 2022, and traders lifted the odds of an October rate hike to 37% from 22%.

briefs.headline: AI stocks crack
briefs.body: The chip index fell for an eighth straight session on Oct 16, the day the Nasdaq 100 shed more than $1 trillion in value. Over the two weeks CoreWeave lost 32.8%, Alphabet 9.9% and Nvidia 5.8%.

briefs.headline: Bonds win the scare
briefs.body: On Oct 22 the 10-year yield fell 19 bp to 4.95%, its biggest one-day drop since March 2023, as investors sold tech and bought Treasuries. On Oct 7 it had touched 5.36%, the highest since 2002.

briefs.headline: Brent tops $116
briefs.body: Brent settled at $116.72 on Oct 23, its highest since April, after Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia and on fears of renewed US strikes on Iran after the Nov 3 midterms. WTI is back above $100.

briefs.headline: Anthropic files to go public
briefs.body: Anthropic filed to list on the Nasdaq as ANT, showing $16.29 billion of first-half revenue, up from $1.16 billion a year earlier. The chip index bounced 2.8% on Monday.

briefs.headline: Apple crosses $5 trillion
briefs.body: Apple went the other way, up 2.2% over the two weeks, and topped $5 trillion in market value for the first time on Oct 14.

earningsLead: Beats did not save the stocks. Four of these five fell the day after reporting.

earnings.line: Revenue beat at $64.60B, but free cash flow went negative, -$2.12B, as capex outran operating cash flow. Stock -7.0%.
EPS beat at $0.87, but it cut its 2026 ad revenue goal to about $2.7B from $3B. Stock -5.3%.
Adjusted EPS of $0.48 beat $0.43; net income fell 29%. Stock -3.1%.
Revenue rose 161% to $14.58B, well above the $12.72B expected. Stock +7.8%, then -9.1% the next day.
A sixth straight record profit, NT$763.1B, up 68.7%. Stock -1.8%.

club.title: Oct 13, earnings basics
club.body: How to read the release, the 10-Q and the call, then bank scorecards for JPMorgan, Wells Fargo, Citi and Goldman.

club.title: Oct 22, Bloomberg intro
club.body: There are 12 Terminals in the Warren Hunting Smith Library. Start Bloomberg Market Concepts (BMC <GO>): about 8 hours, with a certificate.

club.title: Pitches are next
club.body: Member pitches start in the coming weeks and three groups are on the roster. Bring a variant view, three years of numbers, one valuation plus a cross-check, risks, an exit condition, the ask and at least one Bloomberg screenshot.

meetings.what: Eric Stein meeting. No club recap.

items: Fed decision at 2 PM; markets price about an 88% chance of a hold. Alphabet and Microsoft report after the close.
Q3 GDP and September PCE inflation. Amazon reports after the close.
